previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, pacemaker, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, chronic diastolic heart failure, and recurrent left lower extremity cellulitis due to liposclerodermatosis was admitted for worsening erythema, swelling, and pain in her left leg despite prophylactic cephalexin. She was treated with IV vancomycin, showing clinical improvement, and transitioned to oral linezolid for a full 10-day course. A right leg ultrasound ruled out DVT despite calf tenderness and subtherapeutic INR. Warfarin was adjusted cautiously due to prior gastrointestinal bleeding risk. Her pain was managed with a temporary increase in OxyContin, later reduced to baseline, with short-acting oxycodone prescribed for breakthrough pain. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with stable labs, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged with infectious disease and instructions to monitor for recurrence.
